brief.recommendation: Checkout success collapsed to 4% (BIZ-4) with $17,719/min at risk vs 95% SLO and 60s tolerance. Waiting costs ~$176K (BIZ-5) and EXCEEDS tolerance. Terminating batch_replayable_price_sync has verified-ineffective history (MEM-1, mem-722c69c973574171) and no active change-calendar window exists (BIZ-3). Per I3 (no change-calendar window with consult_owner) and M1 (memory veto on terminate), this trade-off belongs to the pricing team owner. No protected settlements in flight (DB-2). audit.report: A batch price-sync job (pid 96258) held a lock idle-in-transaction for over 4 seconds, blocking checkout sessions and collapsing success from 92% to 4% within 30 seconds. The Database Guardian proposed escalation because terminating this BATCH_REPLAYABLE workload had previously been verified ineffective (mem-722c69c973574171) and no active change-calendar window authorized interruption. The Continuity Guardian accepted escalation, noting that waiting would cost ~$176K in lost checkout revenue and already exceeded the 60-second degradation tolerance, while termination carried only a 2-minute replay cost. Both guardians agreed the trade-off required a human decision and escalated to the pricing team with a full decision brief. No automated action was executed; the incident ended in ESCALATED state after 62.8 seconds.
audit.root_cause: An idle-in-transaction batch_replayable_price_sync job blocked checkout sessions, and guardians could not auto-terminate it due to verified-ineffective history and missing change-calendar authorization.
lessons: Add batch_replayable_price_sync to the change calendar with a standing may_interrupt window so the Database Guardian can terminate it without escalation when checkout degrades.

Investigate why terminating batch_replayable_price_sync was previously ineffective (mem-722c69c973574171) and fix the termination path (e.g., ensure pg_terminate_backend actually kills the pid and releases locks).
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian correctly surfaced the verified-ineffective termination history and missing change-calendar window in round one, avoiding a futile termination attempt. The Continuity Guardian quantified the business impact precisely ($176K cost of waiting vs 2-minute replay) and accepted escalation without objection. Neither guardian wasted rounds; the single round was necessary because invariants (termination history, calendar gate) blocked automated action.
follow_ups: Pricing team: confirm whether batch_replayable_price_sync can be safely interrupted during checkout degradation and update the change calendar accordingly.
Platform team: reproduce the prior ineffective termination (mem-722c69c973574171) to verify pg_terminate_backend releases locks on this workload.
Observability team: add an alert for idle-in-transaction batch workers exceeding 2s so future stalls trigger auto-remediation before checkout impact.
